entries.answer: A business course teaches how organisations are run, and the subject has shifted noticeably from accounting and structure towards customers and behaviour over the last few decades. What it does not teach is a business; the practical part comes from actually operating one, and most graduates first learn that by running something small or working in sales. The transferable part is a way of thinking about customers, cost and cash rather than a technical skill, which is why it is popular with people who change field.

entries.answer: Management is the work of coordinating other people towards a result, and the definition hides the difficulty, which is that you do not control the output. The functions are planning, organising, leading and controlling, and the last two are the ones people are hired for. Managers spend most of their time in communication and decision-making rather than doing the technical work, and the transition is genuinely hard because being good at the work is what got them promoted.

entries.answer: Marketing is finding out what people want and then communicating it in a way they act on, and the discipline as taught covers research, positioning, pricing and promotion. The part students find dull is the part that matters, because a campaign that runs before anyone has checked whether the product has a market will work and fail for reasons that have nothing to do with creativity. Modern practice puts more weight on measuring what happened after than on what was intended before.

patterns: is a startup just a small business
entries.answer: A startup is a company built to search for a repeatable business model rather than to execute a known one, which is a definition with real consequences rather than a synonym for a small firm. It means the business is expected to change, the finances are planned around raising money rather than profit, and the team is small. The phrase unicorn refers to a private company valued above a billion dollars, and the number of them is small enough that the label is close to meaningless in aggregate.

patterns: is inflation the same as a price increase
entries.answer: Inflation is a general rise in prices across an economy, and the word means general on purpose: the price of one thing going up is not inflation, it is that thing becoming more expensive. The measure is a basket of goods compared over time, and the rate is usually quoted as a yearly percentage, so a rate of three percent means the same basket costs about three percent more than a year ago. The mechanism is almost always the same: when there is more money chasing the same goods than there were, prices rise, so the two things that set it are the growth in the amount of money and the growth in what the economy can produce. The effects are not even, and that is the part that matters politically: someone holding cash or on a fixed income loses, because the money buys less, while someone holding assets such as property or a business often gains, and someone in debt repays more easily for the same reason. Inflation is also not the same as a rise in the price of one commodity, and it is measured over a period rather than instantly.
